newsitem.title: USA: CIA again probes abuses in Honduras - report.
newsitem.headline: CIA again probes abuses in Honduras - report.

text.p: The CIA's inspector general has reopened an investigation into the failure of agency officers to report allegations of torture by a CIA-supported Honduran military intelligence unit in the mid-1980s, The Washington Post reported in Monday editions.

Quoting unidentified agency officials and congressional sources, the newspaper said Inspector General Frederick Hitz's inquiry raised the possibility of a new round of reprimands or disciplinary actions for active and retired officers for conduct in Central America.
The Honduras investigation was dropped earlier this year but has resumed under pressure from the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, according to the report.

After a similar inquiry last year, two senior Central Intelligence Agency clandestine officers were fired and eight active or former operatives reprimanded for involvement with a Guatemalan army colonel linked to abuses.

The Honduras case centred on a secretive Honduran military unit called Battalion 3-16 which received training and support from the CIA and has been accused of arresting, torturing and "disappearing" suspected leftist subversives in the late 1980s, the Post said.
Hitz's inquiry focused on a CIA case officer in Honduras who allegedly was aware of torture being carried out by the unit but did not report it to headquarters, the report added.

In a separate development, the Post said it had learned that CIA medals were awarded recently to three former top clandestine service officials, each of whom had been disciplined or pushed into retirement in the past two years after reprimands or inspector general inquiries.
The medals were awarded by CIA Director John Deutch and Deputy Director George Tenet "in recognition of long and distinguished careers," the Post said.
